title: Ad of the Week #3: in a gifting ad, write the hook for the giver
hook: In a gifting ad, the buyer and the user are different people.
caption:
In a gifting ad, the buyer and the user are different people.
That changes who the first three seconds should talk to.

Ad of the Week #3 is a pattern, shown on a made-up example: a gifting ad for a candle brand. No real brand and no real results.

A normal product ad answers 'do I want this?'. A gifting ad has to answer the giver's question: 'will they like it, and will it look like I thought about it?'

So the opening names the person receiving the gift. The product arrives as the answer. The giver's worries get handled before the price.

Valentine's briefs get written this month. Swipe for the structure, and one caution from our data.

slides.headline: The gifting ad sells *the person*
slides.sub: A pattern, shown on a made-up example.

slides.headline: Name *who it is for*
slides.body:
A candle brand.

First line on screen: 'For the friend who just moved cities.'

No logo yet and no discount. The giver has already thought of someone before the product appears.

slides.headline: The product arrives as *the answer*
slides.body:
The candle is unboxed in a half-empty flat.

The viewer sees the gift being received. That is the moment the giver is paying for.

Then one reason it suits that person, said once.

slides.headline: Handle the *giver's worries*
items: Will it arrive in time — say the delivery date
Will it look thoughtful — show the unboxing
What if it is wrong — say the exchange rule

slides.headline: Change the *person*, keep the product
items: The friend who just moved cities
The dad who says he wants nothing

slides.headline: less first-month spend for a new message over a *familiar first shot*
slides.sub: So each new person needs a new opening shot, too.
slides.source: Source: Galvor analysis · new video ads launched May–Sep 2026

slides.headline: Write the hook for *the giver*.
slides.sub: Save this before your Valentine's brief.
